Params: Is it really over just like that?
After the two giggling students leave, you and the black-haired girl remain in the plaza, standing in disbelief as you stare at everything in this dream world.
The scene before you is tranquil. The anomaly that just ended has dissolved like a sugar cube in coffee, vanishing without a trace within moments.
What's wrong? Don't tell me even the renowned Commandant of Babylonia is getting attached to this world where all wishes come true?
The girl by your side poses a timely question.
No, it just feels a little... surreal.
I don't think it's quite over just yet.
Then let us go see for ourselves.
The girl walks ahead, the dark blue hem of her skirt fluttering like butterfly wings in the sunset.
After all, compared to simply talking about it, walking around and seeing things for yourself will give you a better sense of what's really going on here.
Speaking of which, there's a movie I've been wanting to see. I heard it's screening at the theater by the subway station.
I needn't say any more, need I, 【kuroname】?
The entrance is plastered with layers upon layers of promotional posters. Instead of removing the old ones, the theater owner simply slapped new posters right over them, it seems.
Finding something worth watching among this mess will be no easy task.
"Love Letter," "Heart Like a Bouquet," "Date A Live"... Hmm, the owner certainly is obvious.
She leans down, carefully sifting through the wall of posters to find a movie she wants to watch.
(...I feel like this is going to take a while.)
(Might as well try contacting Gray Raven now that I've got some free time.)
You take out the communication terminal and attempt to send the message that's been sitting in drafts again.
The girl's face suddenly fills your vision. You see a hint of annoyance in her expression as she leans in and blocks the screen from your view.
Well, you were picking a movie, so I thought...
I might as well try and see if I can reach the outside world one more time.
That won't do. If we're going to watch a movie together, then we're picking it together.
Kurumi takes a step back, though she still plants herself firmly in your line of sight.
Besides, that message won't go through anyway. I've never seen you succeed even once.
The moment she finishes speaking, the terminal in your hand lets out a dull beep, and the text on the screen changes to [Failed to send].
And after witnessing such a "prediction" come true, you can no longer hold back that sense of curiosity gnawing at you.
Why has this girl been acting like she knows you so well from the very moment you met?
Ah, here it is. This is the one I wanted to watch.
The owner is quite the troublesome one, you see. Every time I come here, it takes forever to find what I'm looking for since he always buries the current screenings so deep.
As always, she cuts you off at just the right moment.
The girl tears down her target with pinpoint accuracy from the sea of film advertisements on the wall, then leads 【kuroname】 toward the ticket counter.
You're not sure which movie Kurumi picked in the end.
But as the projector beam flickers to life and the theater falls silent, the answer no longer seems to matter.
The film embodies everything humanity imagines the Golden Age to be—fast-paced, visually stunning, every frame radiating an era's hunger for entertainment and the abundance of ways to satisfy it.
Yet somehow, despite this enticing invitation to indulge, you can't quite fully immerse yourself in this grand audiovisual feast.
...I know what you want to ask, 【kuroname】.
The girl beside you suddenly speaks, her voice so soft it is nearly drowned beneath the theater's lavish surround sound system.
But this movie... is one of the few pleasures I can actually "control" on this long journey.
So for now, please let me finish watching this in peace.
You turn to look at her, and find that Kurumi never shifted her gaze from the screen. Her eyes are fixed on the film even as she speaks.
The projector's glow traces a soft outline along her face. Beneath stray locks of hair, her golden left eye glimmers with a delicate light.
Remember the promise I made to you?
When the time comes, all your questions will be answered.
You nod slightly. An inexplicable sense of reassurance quietly settles over you.

While it is true that you still harbor lingering doubts about this world, as well as many questions about everything that just transpired... It's also true that you have someone trustworthy by your side—an ally you can count on.
In that case, it should be fine to set those worries aside for now.
You still have time to indulge a little before this dream ends, after all.
Aww... I didn't get the one I wanted again.
She cracks open the last capsule. A tiny calico cat charm rests in her palm, but once again, it isn't the one she's been feeding coins into the machine for.
Do you really want the black one that badly?
Yes, now I simply want to get my hands on it, no matter what.
But we've cleared out the whole machine already, and I still didn't manage to get it. I guess... luck just isn't on my side today.
She pats the dust off her skirt and quickly stands up.
Some things just can't be forced. Perhaps Lady Fortune simply isn't looking my way tonight, or perhaps the owner never even put in the black cat to begin with...
All we can do is keep waiting until the next opportunity comes along.
Maybe we can try another convenience store?
We won't know unless we give it a shot.
It's okay. We don't have to make this happen today. "Waiting" is one of my strong suits, after all.
You've grown used to her cryptic, prophetic remarks by now. Nevertheless, when you look up, the sight before you is nothing short of breathtaking.
In the distance, fireworks soar through the night with sharp cracks. Brilliant light shoots skyward, bathing the entire street in flowing and shimmering radiance.

One after another, countless bursts of flame blossom across the sky. Golden, crimson, and aqua light shower the world in a gentle drizzle, transforming into soft, lingering glows right as they reach the ground.
The evening breeze carries with it the faint scent of burnt ash. The sparks flickering across the sky become one magnificent, generous dream, quietly enveloping the night.
Is it some special occasion today? I don't remember getting any notice about this.
Pedestrians gradually gather along both sides of the street, craning their necks upward and whispering amongst themselves.
The girl is still leaning against the railing in front of the convenience store, cradling the small calico cat in her hand. The evening breeze gently lifts the tips of her hair.
Amidst the jostling crowd and the clamor around them, she doesn't look up at the fireworks. Instead, her gaze quietly finds yours.
So, 【kuroname】... Did you have fun in this brief little "dream"?
Her lips curl into a serene smile.
Seeing as you're asking that, though... That means this dream has to end, right?
That's right. After all, our promise hasn't been fulfilled yet.
Like a magician performing a trick, she tucks the calico cat into her pocket and produces a golden pocket watch gleaming with warm light.
Promise me that no matter what happens, don't let it leave your side.
So this is the answer I'm looking for?
It can't answer all your questions just yet, so for now, think of it as a gift in return for the calico cat.
The fireworks fade. She steadies herself against the railing and slowly rises to her feet.
That and... Promise me this as well.
Even if I die "today"—don't try to save me.
Before the weight of her words can even sink in, a flash of sinister light tears through the scenery before you.
A cold gleam cuts into your vision first, followed closely by some warm liquid splattering across your cheek.

An invisible hand reaches out from beyond the door and violently drags the black-haired girl inside. There's no struggle. No scream. Only the sharp sound of tearing can be heard, accompanied by the dull thud of fabric and flesh being ripped apart.
And in that split second, you catch a glimpse of her expression.
Kurumi turns her face slightly to bid you farewell. Her golden left eye, beneath the strands of hair, holds no fear, no pain. It is calm, bordering on tender.
Almost as if... she's experienced this death countless times already.
The only thing your fingertips manage to seize is the fading warmth. Her silhouette sways once in the dark current, then vanishes like fireworks sinking beneath a lake's surface.
Beyond the door, a familiar figure steps into view. Her expression remains serene, yet the smile she wears sends chills down your spine.
I apologize for keeping you waiting.
I'm the one you've been searching for this entire time—"The Oneiros."
